Really enjoying it - everything I loved about the first, but more, better. Really loving the idea of alternate characters and multiple paths! I'm not sure what's up with some of the negative reviews. Like it has co-op?? (https://www.undermine2.game/remote-play) Do people hate Steam Remote Play? I've always thought it was great, since it means there's also a couch co-op option. It's online. It's co-op. I don't understand people. Actually, let me respond to a couple of points in another review, which I think are a little off-base IMO. From another review: "* You will not gain any meta progression, or anything of value at all unless you reach a certain point apparently. You lose =EVERYTHING= when you die. In a run for 30 minutes? Fall into one of way-too-many pits and die? Time is completely wasted. There is no way to leave without hitting this arbitrary point. This is the primary reason for the review." The change here from the first is that gold is now an in-run currency only, meaning you have to clear the second floor (which has the first boss) in order to be guaranteed any thorium or whatever the seal thingies are called for meta progression. That seems... pretty reasonable to me? Literally the only way you're not making any progression at all is if you can't beat the first 10 to 15 minutes of the game. From the other review: "* You start out with a responsive, quick character with a dash as an intro. Then you're given a terrible jumping character with crazy short range. This would be fine (unlockable character upgrades are great) if not for the above point." Since the above point about meta progression doesn't have a lot of merit, all that's left is that yeah, it'll take time to unlock the good stuff. I feel like teasing you in the beginning of a game with a powerful build and then taking it away so you know what you're working towards is a super common trope in games that goes back for decades. Castlevania Symphony of the Night did it. Super Metroid did it. Etc. etc. I do think the movement of Undermine 2 can feel a little bit sluggish when you first start out (similar to Undermine 1), but I think it's promoting a more deliberate style of play rather than hack and slash. It's similar to Hades or Binding of Isaac. From the other review: "* There are way too many enemies, and projectile enemies when spawning into rooms." It's right on par, or probably honestly a little bit easier than Binding of Isaac. But that's why there's a meta progression so you'll get more health and move faster and deal more damage over time, plus get access to new abilities, etc. I don't feel like it's unreasonable, personally. From the other review: "* Enemies do way too much damage (you can take about 7 normal enemy hits, or like... 4 from some). Falling does too much damage." I think maybe this person just was frustrated that they weren't immediately successful at the game? That's what I'm picking up from these complaints. But I feel like enemies doing a lot of damage and forcing deliberate play rather than just running in and killing everything is kind of the hallmark of this genre. Maybe they'd prefer something more like Dynasty Warriors? And again, you will get more HP and get stronger over time through meta-progression. From the other review: "* You will regularly take damage and get hit when entering these over-crowded rooms." I haven't experienced this. If so, that doesn't feel good. But it's EA. Tell the devs? From the other review: "* Healing is incredibly rare ( I saw one drop in 4 runs for 20 health... Basically healing part of a single damage hit)." Healing drops are pretty infrequent. Again, intentional game play. You're not supposed to be running around recklessly and taking a bunch of damage all of the time. That being said, there is a guaranteed store on every floor, and the floor essentially always has at least one healing item. And especially now that gold is an in-run currency, so there's no pressure to save it for meta-progression, you can buy some healing. From the other review: "* No online co-op." It's got remote play: https://www.undermine2.game/remote-play. Anyway, I'm having fun. But I like this kind of game. Clearly it's not for everybody. But if you like roguelites, this is a fun one.

So, I've played Undermine 1 and even 100% it twice, once on Xbox and the other on steam however as excited as i was for Undermine 2 i was simply let down. It's the same items from Undermine 1 with an addition of a few, same blessings with new effects to compensate the Class system they created to make runs more mixed up and even the same..music..just slowed down or altered a slight bit and even the same levels but shorter! and even ALL the same characters and quests. sequels don't have to be entirely new don't get me wrong they can just be better than the original however this just feels like Undermine 1 was remastered graphically and tossed back out as early access because they didn't finish the game most likely by a deadline. The Co-op situation is able to be ignored because i'm fine with doing "local play" via steam remote play however the game was advertised as you playing as rabbit and the peasant not just the same skinned peasants from undermine 1 with no upgrades just new animations. I also don't like that as stated previously it's the same...exact..levels from the 1st game but now only 2 floors a piece? so we get cut content as well? how do we go from 4 floors a level to 2 and not only that but the game became easier! all the enemies are slower, you have significant time to move out the way it almost feels catered to those who cry about games being too hard and they are scared it will chase away business. As far as the complaints of it being repetitive...its a rouge-like..that's what they are so that's kinda user error, however i miss the gold being used to upgrade and continue having it for the next run and losing more and more if i die because there's virtually not enough gold in the now 2 floors of the 1st level to really buy anything in the shop, without spending any gold i end up max with 850 and there's a relic in there for 1125 or 1250. I'n conclusion if you like Undermine and want this...simply go buy the 1st one and play that one instead until this "sequel" is done developing and actually becomes worth buying as a "new game" not just a DLC with better graphics.

[h3] 零创新 [/h3] 1代100%成就260小时，玩了2代直接粉转黑，我所谓的“零创新”，就是字面意义上的真实的纯粹的零创新，靠，全部初代老东西照搬，表面功夫都不带做的换皮都不带换的，还有制作人是对锁眼儿有什么执念？10道门有11道上锁，这他妈和EA没关系吧？和版本没关系吧？上代怎么没这么脑残？纯属找骂。另外我想问问是不是翻译用的不是一代的汉化人员，翻的什么玩意儿，举例——“对敌人的攻击附加中毒”，你要么就“敌人攻击带毒”，要么就“为敌人的攻击附加中毒效果”，这个“对”字用的真好，没玩过的还以为正面效果，人话不会讲，要是纯机翻也就罢了了，明显人翻这种水平当汉化员啊？各种低级错误数不胜数，还把精髓全给丢了，还我白嫖药水！总之，衷心建议新玩家买1，老粉丝勿入，至少再晾个一年再做考虑。难以想象1代称之为同类标杆都不为过的品质，愣是一点儿经验没积累到2上，完全像是换了开发团队，然后重新做了另一个莫名其妙的1代，我不理解的是你都完全照搬了怎么还搬出一大堆前作都不存在的恼人问题。 ✁┄┄✃┄┄✁┄┄✃ ✄╰ひ╯ V0.4——相当不错的大更，我个人是非常认可，尤其是新角色的独特性和趣味。但是如上所述原先的底子太差所以整体分数还是不太上的来，差评暂不作修改。另外这个汉化的问题，真是越更新越翻越烂，要我说干脆1.0之前你就别翻了让大家看英文原版得了反正也不难，翻完反而有阅读障碍，垃圾透了机翻都甩他几条街。

Absolutely not worth it. I'd describe this as "hardcore grind-heavy-for-meta roguelike that thinks constant annoyance and BS is funny". It does everything in its power to annoy and frustrate you CONSTANTLY. Try to get some gold? A slime literally spawns in on it then jumps away, or a big slime spawns and instantly bounces you away from it. Try to hit something with a straight-line projectile? The thing instantly starts strafing and moving diagonally. Thinking the rooms would be well-designed and mostly normal? Nope, there's pits and spikes everywhere coupled with enemies that make YOU strafe, enjoy 15 unavoidable damage as you slide into a pit from being a few pixels too far in one direction. Try to hit something around a corner or against a wall? Your projectile gets deleted because it thinks you're *in* the wall (also applies to corners, which enemies have no trouble hitting YOU around, but your projectiles get instantly deleted if they even get within 10 pixels of one). Try to go in for melee? There's no such thing as melee stagger for nearly every enemy except small green drakes, and you just got hit with a point-blank projectile even though the thing you're hitting was *casting*, and by hardcore logic, should have been interrupted, but no, that logic only applies to YOU and YOU are meant to suffer from it. Want stat-ups? You have to either get lucky, hit enough gold veins, or curse yourself and stack those curses to a point where you're actively hindering your own run to try to make your run passible. The meta-progression is an absolute grind- the purple stuff spawns randomly in levels and guaranteed from boss-kill chests (which only exist because certain curses can turn their keys into other things, you know, to screw you harder) , but you only get about 10 per whole bunch, and smithing relics take 50-110. Crown coins are even worse, you get a whole TWO from the boss chests (and a few from the slime-shop donation box, but that runs out eventually)... and that's the cost of 1 base health or luck up earlygame, but that quickly changes to three-and-up so that you just grind more without ever making much metaprogress. The bosses after Selt are literally just spammy statcheckers/healcheckers- and they deal Contact damage.... and point-blank laser/shoot you with no stagger to stop them... remember that this game is mostly within melee range and "oops your health is gone, sorry nothing"! I'm also just going to flat-out say this: The miners shouldn't be in the game. the lady you do the intro with should have just been the main character, she is LEAGUES better than them, even statwise and %-chance-to-get-blessing-wise - you can stack luck with her meta-upgrades and that does a LOT more than you think it does- reduces shop prices, increases drop rates of EVERYTHING (including the ever-important Potions) , and even gets lots of relics/arcana to be more effective or trigger more because of that luck- she even gets a decent ranged weapon and a true evade-dash instead of a dinky throw that puts you in constant danger that you can't evade from well with a jump that, while it can be used to escape danger, is vertical, not horizontal, and you still have to endanger yourself to do anything as miner anyway, so it ends up being worse than just playing the thief. My suggestions would be: 1. Vastly increase the number of coins/thorium dropped by bosses after the first one. I'm sitting on like 12 blueprints and haven't gotten more than one new relic in 8 runs because not NEARLY enough is dropping at all. Coins too, because you SHOULD get more with how much is perpetually on offer in the hub and needed to progress everything. 2. Bosses need to be toned way the ♥♥♥♥ down. Taking 50 damage because you touched an inactive, immobile orb while trying to focus on meleeing it and dodging other attacks at the same time is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, just like how spamming units on the player (terrible trio boss) while also firing multiple random and unique attacks that all do their own instances of high damage, is also bs. 3. Switch non-corruptive altars and corruptive altars- make the non-corruptive ones common and the corruptive ones more enticing, but rare so that they're actually more worth it and sensical instead of "you have to suffer and survive random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to get the stats you REALLY NEED". 4. Have the forge spawn on every level or at least the ones after the first boss. I don't know why you assume people have 8 bombs+armor+keys by the second level, or why you made the Metal Cubes be the one thing you keep outside of metaprogression, but it's definitely a half-baked feature that encourages banking until you actually start what looks, LOOKS, like a decent run (then it isn't and you feel worse because all the things you forged and the cubes to make them are gone now).

TL;DR: These reviews are crazy. Game is 9/10, EASILY. I absolutely do not understand the negative reviews for this sequel upon EA release. - Build synergy is ridiculously fun and engaging! UM is a game where you have to think about your choices and how you spend your resources. Willy nilly blowing through your keys/bombs/money will not aid you in the long run - Play agency is king! There are like 3 separate mechanics that allow you to craft your build mid-run, and they pop up within a run fairly frequently - Progression is completely fine for the state of release. In fact, progression has more of a metroidvania feel compared to the first - People are saying you don't find items? Seriously?? I am getting between 7-15 items on any given run, and thats NOT including blessings or potions. I would love to see yall's gameplay - Even IF you are having bad luck overall, UM2 is a game that relies on fundamentals. Are you reading the room well? Do you understand order of operations of what to use? Are you cooking food? Are you eliminating threats in an order that makes sense? Are you checking for secret rooms? Etc etc This game's modular and engaging approach to constructing impactful builds is near benchmark level. It pains me to see all the dislike it's garnering considering that I do feel this game is spectacular. Thorium, if you see this review, keep on pushing. This game is a beautiful love letter and is easily shaping up to be one of the best rogue-likes out there

Progression in UnderMine 2 is heavily constrained by its key economy. Each floor effectively requires at least three keys: one for the shop, one for the altar room, and one for the relic room. From the third or fourth floor onward, the game becomes noticeably stingier with key drops, instead flooding runs with bombs or no pickups at all for no reasons. As a result, it becomes practically impossible to access everything a floor offers in later stages. In reality, the required number of keys is even higher, often between five and ten, since many puzzles and optional rewards also consume keys, making an already scarce resource feel artificially rare. In terms of content, a substantial portion of the relics and bosses are carried over directly from UnderMine. Rather than feeling like a true successor, the game comes across as an overpriced DLC. In fact, it feels as though more features from the first game have been removed than genuinely new content has been added. Notably absent are systems such as pet leveling and the sack that allowed players to retain a portion of their gold after death. While this might seem nitpicky for an early access title, these mechanics already existed in the first game, which raises the question of why they are missing here at all. The current development approach gives the impression that content from UnderMine 1 is simply being reintroduced gradually into UnderMine 2, primarily to make it compatible with co-op, a mode that is neither online nor particularly accessible, as it is limited to split-screen play. Appeals to remote play are not especially convincing either, as not every player has a good enough internet connection to make that a viable option. Ultimately, this is still more UnderMine. UnderMine is a good game, and for that reason alone there is enjoyment to be found here. Nevertheless, UnderMine 2 feels uncomfortably close to a lazy cash grab. A cautious approach is strongly recommended: waiting for the full release before deciding whether the amount of new content justifies the steep price seems sensible. Until then, returning to UnderMine 1 is arguably the better option, as the differences are barely noticeable.

[h1] Considering the early access, and how far we are as per 0.6.0 - It's a mighty fine looking ship! [/h1] Yeah, this is definitely an upgrade to Undermine [1] The combat expects you to be familiar with how the dungeons work. The forge is a big recycler of keys, bombs and armour, to produce iron. At first it only accepts keys, then as you unlock the upgrades, you can also choose between smelting bombs and shields into Iron for forge relics or arcanas This game delves deeper than Undermine in a faster fashion, because you're meant to shuffle a few new things... There's lots of strategy that you can still come up with in how to play your current run. The different characters you can play with is pretty much also a big divider between Undermine 1 and 2. Undermine you only had the peasants. So far in this game, you start with Black Rabbit, who's equipped with a throwing dagger and a smaller-than-pickaxe melee. Then you get the peasant, standard miner, pickaxe, and throws like a mathematician. Then you get Dante, who just shows up and swap: You're now Dante, what an exciting WHIP and Dragon breath of fire. Dante ensures you can still cook your dungeon food preventing food poisoning. The game is a great adventure and despite only 2 levels between bosses, the action is in larger rooms with great colour schemes. You're still going to get your familiar places. Delvemore's one of them> But the main reason i got this and i'm already spreading the word is the infinite mode they're bringing with their 0.500 The Well update. Then there was another update The Roost since then, but Steam baited me with the endless mode already here in early access. This developer puts love and passion in their work, and it really shows. The clunky-yet-whimsical mechanics of movement lets you look one direction with your mouse while you're walking another, and it's a hilarious moonwalk, ESPECIALLY when you change rooms while doing it. Please don't ever remove this. The combat shines with you knowing your character and utilising the equipment you're choosing. Every single relic room now has TWO choices. No relic required to get that. There's also a new slot called Arcana's - Basically, the item that will be consuming your mana - Also a new mechanic. Eldertree berries/seeds give you mana - they look like blueberries. +10 per berry, and +30 for a stack. This is such a good game that it still differentiates itself so much from Undermine 1 that you can still enjoy no.1 when you want a change of pace or scenery. CPU and GPU were almost idleing to play this game, it's a really chilled game on the hardware side. There are however, some slowdowns when changing rooms. That's the only time i noticed it, minor, almost irrelevant. In-game also has a super cool report a bug you just noticed window in the options, so it's super useful to help correct things if they really trouble you. The key bindings can be modified as you require it, even allowing multiple binds to one button without notifying you of this, but they will only apply in their respective scenario's - Before you rebind, consider completing at least 3 runs before you do. The arcana's default button is middle mouse click, and you can SPAM it till you have no mana left. You can also quit at the start of a new level and come back at a later stage to continue [like no.1] See update notes: [spoiler] https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1869780/view/519739050796517642?l=english [/spoiler] Some gameplay : [with DnB] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hbj1hgV7EwU&t=41s

Maybe when it gets closer to done? Right now you hit an iron wall when you get to the third tier or so. Very unbalanced. You get hit twice and you're dead by the third tier (library), and with no controls on what you start with any success depends HIGHLY on a very unforgiving RNG. The permanent upgrades are kind of lackluster. 20 more health, 2 more dex, 3 more str. Nothing really game changing especially when you get deeper and you can go from full health to zero in a few seconds. I've gotten all the upgrades for the characters I have unlocked. Fully upgraded you start with 300 health. Drops that increase Str, luck, health, etc. Have been extremely rare in my experience. I might see one or two a run and they'll buff str or int. I have never gotten enough health upgrade drops to offset damage ramping up. Resources like bombs and keys often swings from drought to flood. Secret doors you are supposed to reveal with bombs have no indicators if a bomb doesn't go off in the room first. That's a huge problem when you are in one of those bomb droughts. Regaining mana can also be extremely swingy to the point that I felt anything that used mana was useless and always passed for any upgrade that was just a straight relic. eg. You get a magic item that uses 60-80 mana, you have 100. You can use that thing maybe once in 1-2 levels. There is no natural mana regen and you have to hope mana beads/fruit fall out of stuff you break. Armor is the same way. You get a pip that will take one hit over damage, but replacing it is so rare it is more like a one time shield than not. The first two bosses aren't bad and have some solid pattern memorization with good wind-ups so it never feels cheap fighting them. I can't comment on any further bosses. I keep getting murdered within a few seconds of entering the first room with mobs in the library. Full health -> No health game over. Once or twice, I could see as a skill issue but I've put several hours into it and there are no upgrades left to buy. Unlocked some church dude with a whip who really just sucks even with all the upgrades. It's terrible trying to aim the whip and his fire does equally low damage. Bought some upgrades that mentioned something about shockwaves but I can't tell that it made a difference with him. The game says something about seeds, but I'm not sure what it would do since it's all random every time anyway. Shouldn't the seed change with every game? Read some discussions on the forum indicating you need to do a bunch of fail runs and save blue prints/plans and build specific starting artifacts with the purple metal you find to start a run you want to try and progress on... that seems like ♥♥♥♥ way to build a game. Every run should be able to be a progression run and saving and expending resources across a few runs so you can make one good attempt then have RNG smite your run with something stupid like three dragons hitting you and once. TLDR: The game depends too highly on RNG and the mob damage is overtuned. Not fun.

Title: A step back from the original's addictive loop I thoroughly enjoyed the original UnderMine and was looking forward to the sequel, but unfortunately, this title falls short of its predecessor’s high standards. While the early-game progression feels satisfying and fast-paced, the pacing hits a wall after a few hours. I managed to max out all weapon and armor upgrades relatively quickly, but after that, the upgrade path becomes opaque and stagnant. There is a lack of clear direction or meaningful scaling for the subsequent tiers of progression, leaving the character feeling static. The core gameplay loop is hampered by tedious map navigation. Too often, runs devolve into mindless backtracking across the map, hunting for a specific key to unlock a door that gated progress. This design choice makes individual runs feel bloated and artificially prolonged, transforming what should be an exciting roguelite experience into a repetitive and boring chore. I hope the developers address these pacing and navigation issues in future updates, as the foundation doesn't currently live up to the first game.

Sounds are very distinct from one another, almost all are on point and work well providing you a decent insight in what is going on, what your character is doing and which enemy is doing what, when. So far well done. Character sound design is pretty decent, everything runs on cue and makes sense and each playable character having their very distinct set works well. The familiars are also on point. It's probably a choice of the game developers to make the characters scream in agony when jumping through the hole towards the next layer, i would have done it differently and brought more excitement and pomp into it, i am here to conquer a dungeon, not be scared of it. The music is well done and the flows from neutral to combat to entering specialty rooms are great to decent. Now that the new patch releases a new playable character releases, once i unlocked this character i went out to explore the dungeon with this Minerva. And in simple words all i can say is that Minerva sounds out of place in such a way that it turns me off from playing the game, i tried to play Minerva and Minerva's gameplay-mechanic is nice and I can already see some great combo's with relics and arcana, yet every time Minerva gets either hit, jumps down the hole or does a melee attack the enjoyment of playing the game just gets bombed like i am falling out of love with someone. Eventually i let Minerva die in the Dining hall. All i know for now is that when i think about the game i not only hear the main song, which is fine, yet Minerva's sound is now haunting throughout it and i just can't. I will still leave a positive recommendation, it's the first iteration of undermine i played so am unable to compare it to the first installment, yet with this update, for now i am out.

Verdict: Undermine 2 is great, but it is pretty dishonest about how much content is recycled from the first game, which, at this point, is just superior in terms of available content. I would say 'Wait for full release' is fair recommendation Honestly, when I buy a new game or a sequel, I am not expecting for it to be 40% copy pasted content with zero to no changes and certainly not main, unavoidable bosses. + Positives + + Steam achievements (53, a lot are luck based) + 4 playable characters + The game looks great + Tons of items + Branching paths + New quests and items in the hub + Endless mode – Negatives – - No steam trading cards (yet) - Item balance is all over the place - No journal - No option to ban unlocked items (and a lot of them are useless for most runs) - Recycled content from the first game (items, locations, monsters, - Selt, Mortar and Noori are copy pasted from Undermine 1 - Hard cap on some meta resources - New recipes won't drop until you craft the old ones - Character balance is all over the place honestly
